deities: Lord Shiva (Mahadev; local belief calls the linga swayambhu/self-manifested - verify)

history.period: Origins unclear; one travel listing claims the temple is about 1000 years old (verify); local legend treats it as swayambhu
history.summary: Garadia Mahadev is a small clifftop Shiva shrine on the edge of the Chambal gorge, roughly 20-28 km south of Kota city off NH-76 toward Dabi and Chittorgarh (verify distance). The Chambal river bends in a horseshoe through a deep gorge here, and the viewpoint is among Rajasthan's most photographed landscapes; it came into prominence after featuring in Rajasthan Tourism advertisements around 2016 and after the song 'Man Bharya' was shot there (verify song claim - from a travel blog). The shrine is reached by descending a few steps; a small stream flows from a hole in the rock beside it (verify). It lies inside/near a forest area: a 2017 visitor report describes passing a forest check post and paying an entry fee (verify current fee and access rules). FLAG: coordinates here are from OpenStreetMap/Rajasthan Tourism listings for the gorge temple (25.11721, 75.72959); the geocoder's match for the name points to a different same-named temple inside Kota city (Talwandi) - do not use that. District flag: most sources say Kota; Rajasthan Tourism's address reads 'Garadiya Mahadev Rd, Talera Tehsil' (Talera is a Bundi-district tehsil) - verify whether the temple falls in Kota or Bundi district.

name: Garadia Mahadev Temple
town: Near Dabi, south of Kota (CSV town 'Kota' is the nearest city; the gorge temple is ~20-28 km from Kota city on the NH-76 Chittorgarh road)
town_description: The Garadia Mahadev shrine sits on a cliff on the edge of the Chambal gorge, roughly 20-28 km south of Kota city on the NH-76 road toward Dabi and Chittorgarh. At this point the Chambal river takes a horseshoe bend through a deep, cliff-flanked gorge - a landscape often compared to Gandikota. The area is semi-wild (visitors report leopard sightings nearby) and remains relatively off the mainstream tourist circuit; the spot is also popular for picnics, photography and sunrise/sunset viewing.

travel.airport: Kota airport has no scheduled commercial flights (verify); nearest major airports are Jaipur (~250 km) and Udaipur (~250 km) - verify distances.
travel.railway: Kota Junction, about 25-30 km away (verify); taxi or private vehicle needed from the station.
travel.road: Detour off NH-76 (Kota-Chittorgarh) near Dabi, about 20-28 km from Kota; the last stretch is narrow rural road. A 2017 report mentions a forest check post with an entry fee - verify current fee and access rules before visiting.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; monsoon (July-September) is scenic but the gorge and forest tracks can be slippery - verify whether access is restricted then.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Rajasthan Tourism listing: 7:00 AM - 5:30 PM daily (verify); one travel listing says 5:00 AM - 7:00 PM (verify). The priest generally leaves around 5:30 PM; late evenings not recommended.
